verbatimHtmlExcerpts: The calculations in the NOAA Sunrise/Sunset and Solar Position Calculators are based on equations from Astronomical Algorithms, by Jean Meeus.

Please be advised that the NOAA/GML Solar Calculator is no longer actively supported or maintained by our team. While the calculator remains available for use, we cannot guarantee its accuracy or functionality and will not be providing updates or technical support.

Please note that calculations in the spreadsheets are
only valid for dates between 1901 and 2099, due to an approximation used in the
Julian Day calculation. The web calculator does not use this approximation,
and can report values between the years -2000 and +3000.

The approximations used in these programs are very good for years between
1800 and 2100.

applicationPolicy.calendar: proleptic Gregorian; actual Unix epoch -> JD (no spreadsheet approximation); corrected wall coordinates may enter adjacent 1899 or 2101
applicationPolicy.equationOfTimeSign: apparent solar time minus mean solar time
applicationPolicy.formula: apparent solar wall coordinate = actual UTC epoch + 4 * eastLongitude minutes + EOT minutes
applicationPolicy.civilCorrectionFormula: 4 * eastLongitude - actual IANA UTC offset minutes + EOT
applicationPolicy.boundaryWindowMeaning: product review window, not a certified error bound; does not itself withhold a chart
applicationPolicy.secondsMeaning: display resolution only; not observational accuracy; floor the fractional wall coordinate to the preceding second, never round across a boundary
applicationPolicy.excluded: Sunrise/sunset, latitude, topocentric observer corrections, Delta-T/UT1 correction, atmospheric refraction and any claim of traditional-method efficacy
